messages:
ashok: quick Q — I only have a request_identifier `af3b2c7` and a trace id `01-abcdef123`. Trying to pull the full request log in staging, fastest path?
maria: open Trace Viewer (https://console.redwood.internal/traces) and paste the trace id — it usually shows a Logs panel that links to Kibana. If the trace is missing spans, fallback to logs search by request_identifier.
tim: CLI quick path: console search -> paste request_identifier. If you prefer terminal tails, use stern on the runtime pods and grep the id.
sasha: commands I use (staging):
```
# list recent runtime pods
kubectl -n staging get pods -l app=runtime
# tail logs and filter for the request id (live)
stern -n staging runtime -c runtime --since 5m | grep af3b2c7 --line-buffered
# look up archived logs in ES (internal API)
curl -s 'https://logs.internal.redwood/_search' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query": {"match": {"request_id": "af3b2c7"}}}'
```
maria: console -> Requests explorer also works: paste request_identifier and click the row to get model/context + trace link. If the request was sampled out from tracing, the console search still finds the log lines.
ashok: nice. any gotchas? what if trace link just 404s?
tim: 404 usually means the span wasn't ingested or trace retention expired. Check the pod logs around the timestamp. Also check tracing-proxy logs for dropped spans.
deploy-bot: FYI: staging logs retention = 14 days. If older than that, try S3 archive: s3://logs-archive/staging/YYYY/MM/DD or contact infra.
sasha: we have a small helper script if you want to automate both checks:
```
# tools/find_request.sh --env staging --id af3b2c7
# It calls console API, then falls back to stern if needed and prints links.
```
maria: if you still can't find anything ping me and include the exact timestamp for the request and the pod name (if known). Also paste the console query you used.
ashok: will do — trying now, i'll report back. thx everyone :rocket:
